name: Online Passive Income
goal: Build an AI-assisted Digital Product Studio that discovers, validates, designs, builds, tests, prepares and (with explicit approval) publishes digital products across B2C, B2B and prosumer markets, targeting €1,000/month within five years.

hypotheses.name: Low-friction life-admin toolkit
hypotheses.audience: Consumers who struggle with planning and recurring admin
hypotheses.format: Interactive web tool or simple spreadsheet/template
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Existing planning systems can be too complex to start and maintain; a narrow tool may reduce setup and decision friction.
hypotheses.validation: Find first-hand complaints, compare free alternatives, test a clickable/manual prototype and price acceptance.

hypotheses.name: Simple personal-finance decision calculator
hypotheses.audience: Consumers managing irregular expenses, budgets or savings goals
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: People need a clear answer to a specific money decision without setting up a full finance app.
hypotheses.validation: Identify one repeated decision, check existing free calculators and test usefulness with target users.
hypotheses.note: Illustrative hypothesis only; avoid regulated financial advice.

hypotheses.name: Modular wedding planning toolkit
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Generic mega-planners can be unwieldy; separate guest, budget, vendor and seating workflows may be easier to use.
hypotheses.validation: Investigate specific spreadsheet failure points and test one module rather than a broad planner.
hypotheses.note: Illustrative hypothesis only; existing free tools are strong substitutes.

hypotheses.name: Freelancer scope and pricing calculator
hypotheses.format: Interactive calculator and client-ready scope summary
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Scope creep and unclear change requests can turn into unpaid work; a lightweight estimator/change-order workflow may help.
hypotheses.validation: Research repeated first-hand examples, existing contracts/calculators and willingness to pay.

hypotheses.name: Micro-business admin workflow kit
hypotheses.audience: Solo operators and small service businesses
hypotheses.format: Templates, calculators and lightweight workflow tool
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Recurring invoicing, reminders, quoting and record reconciliation create admin burden.
hypotheses.validation: Choose one narrow recurring workflow; map current tools and test whether owners pay to remove it.
hypotheses.note: Illustrative hypothesis only; do not handle payments or sensitive records in the first MVP.

hypotheses.name: Creator workflow utilities
hypotheses.audience: Independent creators and small content businesses
hypotheses.format: Content planning, pricing or asset workflow tool
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Creators repeatedly coordinate content, client work and deliverables across disconnected tools.
hypotheses.validation: Look for one measurable bottleneck with existing spend or workaround.

hypotheses.name: Small Café Manager Starter Kit
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Simple operational systems may save owner/manager time.
hypotheses.validation: Existing initial scan only; free substitutes are strong and willingness to pay is unproven.
hypotheses.note: Keep as one vertical, not the studio's exclusive market.

hypotheses.name: ShiftBrief AI
hypotheses.problem_hypothesis: Important shift notes and tasks can be missed in fragmented communication.
hypotheses.validation: Existing initial scan only; competitors exist and willingness to pay/adoption is unproven.
hypotheses.note: Keep as one vertical, not the studio's exclusive market.

phases.name: Existing workflow foundation
phases.goal: Private repository, deterministic orchestration, scheduled RSS discovery, reports, dashboard and spend guardrails; this is not yet an autonomous LLM studio.

phases.name: Cross-market opportunity discovery
phases.goal: Scan B2C, B2B and prosumer markets; collect competitor, pricing, pain-point and substitute evidence; score evidence quality.

phases.name: Demand validation and opportunity selection
phases.goal: Narrow the best candidates, identify target users, test current workarounds and willingness to pay before committing to a build.

phases.name: Product requirements and design
phases.goal: Create a concise PRD, user journey, prototype, acceptance criteria and smallest useful MVP.

phases.name: Product development
phases.goal: Build a working product in its own product folder with reproducible setup and documentation.

phases.name: Quality assurance
phases.goal: Test core flows, edge cases, accessibility, mobile usability, privacy and reliability.

phases.name: Sales and launch assets
phases.goal: Prepare product name, positioning, screenshots, instructions, pricing hypothesis, support and listing copy.

phases.name: Approval and publication
phases.goal: Review platform fees, tax/VAT, privacy and listing details; publish only after explicit user approval.

phases.name: Analytics and iteration
phases.goal: Measure visits, conversion, refunds, support and revenue; improve, reposition or stop products based on evidence.

phases.name: Autonomous studio capability
phases.goal: Implement and integrate guarded role-based AI dispatch with offline default, structured outputs, human approval gates, spend enforcement, persistence and evaluations. Live paid inference remains disabled until explicit approval.

tools_to_evaluate.name: Haimaker AI
tools_to_evaluate.reason: User found the service and wants to assess possible future usefulness.

preliminary_assessment.potential_fit: Later LLM backend/model gateway for the agent or an AI-powered product; not required for the current deterministic agent and not a customer-facing app host.
preliminary_assessment.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-token pricing; free signup does not mean ongoing free inference. Check live model rates and any deposit/credit conditions before use.
preliminary_assessment.privacy_caution: Privacy policy states prompts and responses are logged by default and deleted after 30 days; opt-out is available in API key settings. Third-party model providers' own policies also apply.
preliminary_assessment.decision: Watchlist only. No signup, integration, data upload, API key or payment without explicit approval.

guardrails: Do not subscribe to, integrate, connect accounts to, or upload private project data to Haimaker AI without checking it and receiving explicit user approval.
Netlify auto-publishing remains locked; no unlock, deploy, or plan change without explicit user approval.
The studio explores B2C, B2B and prosumer markets; specialty coffee and hospitality are only two candidates, not the exclusive focus.
No product candidate is considered validated from search volume, competitor listings, anecdotes or model-generated scores alone.
Build and publish one real product through the full lifecycle; do not keep expanding infrastructure without producing customer-facing value.
Create products in private repository workspaces first. Public launch, paid services, account changes and customer outreach require explicit user approval.

strategy.operating_model: Portfolio-first studio: discover opportunities across multiple markets; score evidence; select one narrow problem; ship a small useful product; measure real buyer behaviour; repeat.
audiences: Prosumer freelancers, creators and independent professionals
strategy.product_principle: Simple to understand, immediately usable, low-friction onboarding, focused on a concrete job rather than a generic template or generic AI wrapper.
strategy.decision_rule: No idea is considered validated based on search volume, competitor presence, community anecdotes or AI-generated scores alone. Seek evidence of repeated pain, existing workarounds/spend and willingness to pay.

first_mvp_candidate.name: ScopeSnap
first_mvp_candidate.job: Turn an out-of-scope client request into a clear, priced change proposal before extra work starts.
first_mvp_candidate.format: No-login browser utility that calculates additional fees/time and creates a client-ready change summary.
first_mvp_candidate.confidence: Low-to-moderate; repeated qualitative pain signals and competitor evidence exist, but direct interviews, willingness-to-pay and conversion remain untested.
first_mvp_candidate.reason: Narrow and fast to prototype; avoids bank, accounting, email and contract integrations; useful output immediately; can be tested with a free prototype.
first_mvp_candidate.validation_gate: Observe 5–8 freelancers using the prototype; measure whether they can create and would send a change request; ask what they currently use and whether they would pay for export/templates or team features.
